mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS increases, or the 3-month FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when controlling for PAYEMS and UNRATE movements.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog but proxy via HOUST for industrial demand) followed by a decline in the producer price index (INDPRO) indicates a shift from demand-driven to cost-driven inflation, which tends to reduce equity risk premia and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive despite the described HOUST/INDPRO pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the goods price index (INDPRO) below 102 signals excess supply in the economy, lowering growth expectations and equity valuations, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days when triggered by a falling CPIAUCSL.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by > 1% while INDPRO < 102 over the same horizon
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO < 102 and CPIAUCSL decline.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform in the next 20-day window due to higher risk-free rates compressing equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns exceed +1% during the high-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable) inferred from a sharp increase in PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE suggests tight labor markets, which can fuel inflation and equity volatility, often producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.3 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive despite the described PAYEMS/UNRATE pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in consumer spending proxies (e.g., HOUST) followed by a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from demand to supply constraints, which can lead to a sharp S&P 500 decline in the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 8% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by > 2% over the next month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-COVID recovery phase (regime: 'post-pandemic normalization'), a combination of rising consumer confidence (implied via CPIAUCSL acceleration) and easing monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 5%) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate > 2% monthly and FEDFUNDS < 5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the specified regime.
